items.item_text: Active California Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) certification. In lieu of a CNA licensure, enrollment in a nursing program with a minimum one completed med/surg rotation can be substituted, and proof of either must be provided upon hire.
Current BLS certification from the American Heart Association
Previous experience in a Central Monitoring Unit (CMU) or Video Monitoring Unit (AvaSure/CareView)
Prior work experience in acute care, intermediate care, or telemetry settings

Under the direction of the CMU Supervisor and Unit Director, the Per Diem Admin Clinical Care Partner / Video Monitor Tech plays a key role in supporting patient safety and continuous observation across UCLA Health campuses. In this 6-hour shift role, you will provide break relief coverage for both video (AvaSure/CareView) and ECG monitoring, ensuring uninterrupted surveillance and timely communication of patient safety concerns or rhythm changes.

Working closely with the Central Monitoring Unit (CMU) team, you’ll promptly notify the assigned RN of any changes in patient condition via Epic Secure Chat or phone, helping to maintain the highest standards of clinical vigilance and care. Your commitment to attentiveness, teamwork, and communication will directly contribute to our mission of delivering safe, reliable, and patient-centered care.

At UCLA Health, you’ll be part of an organization nationally recognized for nursing excellence, where your work supports the health system’s mission, values, and CICARE standards of compassionate, connected care.
May convert to a career opportunity*
EKG Cardiac Monitor tech; capable of analyzing EKG arrythmia - highly preferred
Shift: Minimum of two 6-hour shifts per week (9:30 PM – 4:00 AM, including coverage for breaks and transitions)
Nights: Variable (Sunday–Saturday); minimum of two weekend shifts per 4-week schedule period
Reports to: CMU Supervisor / Unit Director
This position could have the potential to float between the UCLA Health Santa Monica Medical Center, UCLA Health West Valley Medical Center, and the UCLA Health Ronald Regan Westwood Medical Center.
Strong attention to detail, communication, and multitasking skills
Familiarity with Epic or other electronic health record communication platforms
Ability to maintain focus and situational awareness in a high-volume monitoring environment
